explanation: A subarray ending at prefix j is valid when its starting prefix is at least prefix[j]−k. The running maximum of prefixes is sorted; binary search finds the earliest such start, even when array entries are negative.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: A subarray from prefix index i to j has sum prefix[j]−prefix[i], so it qualifies exactly when prefix[i]≥prefix[j]−k. The first running-prefix maximum meeting this threshold occurs at the earliest actual qualifying prefix. Binary search finds that earliest start for every end, giving the longest valid interval despite negative entries.
walkthrough: For [4,−6,3,1] with k=0, the full sum is 2 and is invalid. The suffix [−6,3,1] sums to −2 and has length 3, longer than any other qualifying subarray.
edgeCases: Negative entries prevent the usual positive-only sliding-window rule.
If no nonempty interval qualifies, return 0.
Long prefix sums avoid intermediate int overflow.
